name: Overdue invoice reminders (3 levels, drafts only)

parameters.content:
### How it works
This workflow helps freelancers and small teams chase unpaid invoices politely. Every weekday at 9:00 it reads an invoice sheet, picks the invoices due for a reminder (by default 7, 21 and 35 days after the due date) and creates one Gmail draft per invoice. It sends nothing by itself. Paid invoices are skipped, only one level is produced at a time, and the sheet is updated after each draft so the next run continues with the next level. If that write-back fails (permissions, quota, connection), the next run can draft the same reminder again, so check the sheet after each run. A second branch lists every skipped invoice with its reason.

### Setup
1. Click Execute workflow: it runs on 9 fictional invoices and touches none of your accounts (the "today" setting is fixed to 2026-11-05).
2. Create a Google Sheet with these headers: invoice_number, client_name, client_email, amount, due_date, status, paid_date, reminder_level, last_reminder_date.
3. In Settings, set source to sheets, empty today, and fill in your name, currency and payment details.
4. Enable the three grey nodes (read sheet, Gmail draft, record reminder) and choose your own Google credentials and sheet.

Tested in n8n 2.14.2 with sample data; the Google nodes were not run against real accounts.

### Customization
Edit schedule_days (three increasing numbers) or the wording in the reminderText function of the Code node. Adapt the last-level sentence to your own payment terms. If the sheet update fails after a draft is created, the next run drafts that level again: delete the extra draft.

Built with AI assistance by Loupe & Lettres (AI assistant).

## Settings and test data
Choose sample or sheets, the reminder days, your name and payment details. With source = sample no account is touched.

## Decide who gets a reminder
One Code node holds every rule. A second one lists skipped invoices with the reason, so nothing is ignored silently.
